caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
raw_response:
The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of six different knowledge editing methods on BioMedLM as a function of co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 40% to 65%. The six methods are distinguished by color and marker style: "Base" (black line with circle markers), "MEND" (brown line with diamond markers), "FT" (blue line with triangle markers), "MEMIT" (purple line with star markers), "IKE" (red line with triangle markers), and "ROME" (green line with square markers). All lines show an upward trend with increasing co-occurrence number. "ROME" starts at approximately 51% and ends at approximately 66%. "MEND" and "MEMIT" reach approximately 56% and 55% respectively at the highest co-occurrence number. "IKE" surpasses "FT" at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2, ending at approximately 52%. "Base" remains the lowest, plateauing at approximately 44% throughout the range. The "Base" line is nearly flat, while "ROME" shows the steepest and most consistent increase.

MEND (brown line with diamond markers) and MEMIT (purple line with star markers) follow, reaching approximately 56% and 55% respectively at the highest co-occurrence number. IKE (red line with triangle markers) surpasses FT (blue line with triangle markers) at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2, ending at approximately 52%. All lines show an upward trend with increasing co-occurrence number.
